source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 3.2, Proposition 1; Section 3.3, Proposition 2 and equations (9)–(10)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Proposition 1 states stochastic domination of the selective randomization p-value and selective type-I-error control; Proposition 2 gives the conditional selective randomization distribution and its computable form when the relevant objects are imputable.

Theorem 2 is a random-partition multivariate finite-population CLT and Theorem 4 is a multivariate completely randomized-experiment CLT; neither is a selected, data-dependent-reference transfer theorem.

source_verification_receipts.version: preprint corresponding to Annals of Statistics 46 (2018), 679–710
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 9 is a selective central-limit theorem for linearizable statistics with randomized selection and smooth likelihood conditions under independent sampling.
Theorem 1 represents discretized adaptive policies; the paper solves sparse-program design problems under model-based operating-characteristic constraints.
The paper establishes Ehrhard–Borell inequality/equality results, rather than selected-score quantile or enrichment-design claims.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv v2, revised 16 January 2026; unpublished preprint
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: This is available as a non-archival preprint concerning optimal conditional inference in batched Gaussian adaptive experiments; it is used only as adjacent context and not as a basis for an N-flag.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define the fiber as an explicit measurable set of complete chronological assignment histories, listing exactly which selector, recruitment, statistic, and assignment-probability values it preserves; state the Rbase selection-margin bound uniformly almost surely over its realized datasets.

Correct every Freidling comparison to distinguish Proposition 1’s validity result from Proposition 2’s conditional-law/computability result, and anchor the flagship transfer and holdout claims to Section 5’s stated future directions.

Make thm:negative-interior explicitly conditional on, and dependent on, thm:uniform-selected-transfer, or restate it purely as a theorem of the declared Gaussian experiment before using it as the finite-population counter-regime.

Concentrate the field contribution on the transfer theorem plus certified holdout optimizer, and demote the Ehrhard-derived convexity, proportional special case, and generic interval machinery to supporting results unless they deliver an independently nonroutine equality characterization.

recommended_next_step: Revise the reference-fiber semantics, selection-margin quantification, dependency chain, and Freidling attribution, then return the repaired field-tier transfer-and-optimizer kernel to Stage 0.
